notes:
### Signals reads exposure, the assistant keeps its work, and a Mac cannot be run out of memory

- **Signals now reads exposure and colour on every frame.** Each clip gets
  a luma curve and events at frame precision: a step (the operator changed
  exposure, a light switched), a fast ramp (iris hunting, a fade), a slow
  drift (a sunset, a timelapse), flicker, a white-balance or grade change,
  and stretches of blown highlights or crushed blacks. Clean ranges split
  at every step and leave out fast ramps and flicker, so the assistant and
  the rough cut pick either side of a change instead of across it. The
  curve is drawn in the clip inspector under motion, and every clip the
  assistant reads carries the events and the curve. Existing footage gets
  it on the next Rescan Signals; new ingests get it on the way in.
- **Every Signals pass has its own switch** under Settings, Analysis,
  Signals, each hint saying what turning it off costs.
- **A long Rich Describe run cannot exhaust a Mac any more.** The describe
  process releases its working memory after every clip, is restarted
  automatically when it grows or after 150 clips (without re-calibrating),
  and the app logs its memory every few minutes; the diagnostics bundle
  carries the last 24 hours of that curve.
- **The assistant keeps its material and its cap keeps its work.** A build
  no longer re-reads the same transcripts because older tool replies were
  collapsed; a re-fetched reply is kept, transcripts stay whole, the cap
  is 20 steps per send (a settings row now), the last step writes down
  where it got to, and "keep going" continues from there instead of
  re-buying the reads. The cap message shows what the send cost.
- **A project's local brain is the brain that is called.** Chat, the
  planners and every text job follow the project's pill; a project set to
  a local model no longer sends its footage to a cloud provider.
- **Timeline updates keep their backup.** An update stops before deleting
  anything when Resolve refuses the backup duplicate or the target will
  not become current, and failed attempts no longer leave a spare backup
  timeline behind.
- **Timeline tabs open the document they are named after** whatever tabs
  you closed, and a cut the assistant just made becomes the active tab
  (shoot-day timelines built in the background never steal focus).
- **Assistant panel:** bubbles follow the panel width, and the composer
  grows to half the panel as you type.
- **Tech stack tells the truth about keys.** Rows refresh when a key is
  entered, the doubled rows that could never update are fixed, and
  "Refresh models" lists the live OpenAI and Google catalogues so new
  models appear without an update.
- **Filing sheet:** the folder box no longer collapses when its clock line
  lands; a file filed with None stays that way after a restart; a skipped
  file is not offered again by the watch folder; the sheet grows with its
  rows.
- **The Dropbox lease message on a single machine is fixed.** The lease
  identifies the install rather than the computer's network name, which
  a Mac laptop changes on a Wi-Fi hop, and the message only mentions
  Dropbox when the library really is on a synced folder.
- **Audio, Resync and Archive:** audio cannot be imported into the wrong
  Resolve project, audio rows are marked synced only after Resolve takes
  them and Resync imports the ones it skipped, Resync recovers an offline
  ingest in one press and honours "don't build timelines", and the Archive
  page's Send to project targets the project you picked, keeps same-named
  clips apart, plays a result from its own drive and keeps a moment's
  in and out marks.
- **Money:** the monthly cap counts Gemini and Perplexity, prices an
  unknown paid model conservatively, and treats OpenRouter's free tier as
  free. The time remaining on a lane follows the run's recent pace instead
  of standing still.
- **Windows:** no child process can flash a console window.
- **Test bundles never land on the developer's Desktop, and the test suite
  runs entirely headless.**
